name: v5 / P2: support-aware (trust-gated) hurdle-aware correction
frozen: 2026-11-09, before any P2 computation on any slide
question: When the measured cores miss some tissue states, does a correction learned from them harm cells unlike the cores, and does gating the correction by support distance prevent that?
base: HAC from config_v4.json (unchanged); zero-shot fallback S = q * relu(mu) (GHIST+-Soft)

trust_gate.state_space: 10 principal components of the soft score S standardised over all slide cells (PCA fitted on 50,000 random cells, seed 0); RNA-free
trust_gate.support_distance: d_i = mean Euclidean distance to the 10 nearest core cells in that space
trust_gate.reference: d_ref = 95th percentile of leave-one-core-out distances (each core's cells to the cells of the other cores; a single core uses its 4 angular sectors)
trust_gate.tuned_parameters: none (k = 10, 95th percentile, exponent 2 fixed in advance)

amendment_1.date: 2026-11-09, after one Breast5K smoke run (tumour_biased, seed 0), before any full P2 run and before any ATERA computation
amendment_1.reason: The frozen gate mixed two outputs on different scales (calibrated HAC vs uncalibrated S). With only 3% of cells gated, the all-cell median PCC fell from 0.089 to 0.075, because splicing differently-scaled values breaks each gene's ranking. That is a design bug, not a tuning issue.
amendment_1.change: The gate now acts only on HAC's multigene occurrence correction, which is the extrapolating part: q_trust = q + lambda * (q_hat - q); output = q_trust * m_hat, where m_hat is HAC's per-gene magnitude map. lambda, d_ref, k, the percentile and the exponent are unchanged. The fallback at lambda = 0 is GHIST+'s own occurrence with the core-calibrated per-gene magnitude ('GHIST+-q-mag', also reported).

amendment_2.date: 2026-11-09, after a second Breast5K smoke run (tumour_biased, seed 0); still before any full P2 run or any ATERA computation. FINAL: no further changes; the full results are reported whatever they show.
amendment_2.reason: HAC's occurrence correction has two parts: q_hat = q + c + (X - xm) W. c is a per-gene intercept, a global recalibration that corrects GHIST+'s inflated occurrence probabilities everywhere, and it is not extrapolation. (X - xm) W is the multigene, cell-specific part. Gating both sent gated cells back to the inflated raw q (all-cell median PCC 0.089 -> 0.081 with 3% of cells gated).
amendment_2.change: q_trust = q + c + lambda * (X - xm) W, clipped to [0.001, 0.999]; output = q_trust * m_hat. The fallback at lambda = 0 ('GHIST+-q-mag') is now q + c with the core-calibrated magnitude.

settings.unbiased: 4 x 1 mm2 diverse cores (identical to the v3/P1 primary config)
settings.tumour_biased: 4 x 1 mm2 cores drawn at random (seeded) from the 25% of 400 candidate disks with the highest mean GHIST+-predicted Malignant+Epithelial probability; RNA-free
settings.stroma_biased: same, from the 25% of candidates with the lowest mean Malignant+Epithelial probability

evaluation.cells: v3 rule: every cell > 200 um from all core edges
evaluation.metrics: median per-gene PCC (all genes) and mean RMSE per subset; block-bootstrap (400 um blocks, 500 resamples) 95% CI of HAC-trust minus HAC median PCC, on out-of-support cells and on all cells

decision_rule: P2 is useful if, in the biased settings on both slides, (i) HAC is worse than GHIST+-Soft on out-of-support cells in the mean over repeats (the problem exists), and (ii) HAC-trust beats HAC on out-of-support cells with the CI excluding 0 in >= 2 of 3 repeats; and in the unbiased setting HAC-trust's all-cell median PCC is within 0.002 of HAC. If (i) fails, P2 is reported as unnecessary on these slides. Everything is reported either way.
